6. Cotton Export Corporation (Cotton Export Corporation)

The Government of Pakistan established this corporation in November 1973 for the export of cotton, which has played an important role in increasing the export of local cotton.

7. Trade relations with Muslim countries

The Government of Pakistan has tried very much to promote trade relations with the Muslim countries of Asia and Africa. Thus our trade with Islamic countries is increasing.

8. Finance for the export of local machinery

To increase the export of machinery prepared within the country, the State Bank, through commercial banks, provides loans at a low rate of interest to traders exporting such machinery, because of which the export of such machinery has been encouraged.

9. Import of machinery

Industries preparing exportable goods (e.g. textiles, leather, sports goods, surgical instruments, utensils, cutlery and furniture) have been given permission to import machinery from outside on paying 35 per cent duty. In this way the export capacity of these industries will increase.

10. Membership of world trade organisations

Pakistan has adopted the membership of different world trade organisations so that it can promote its trade. Among them these are especially noteworthy: the General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs (GATT), the World Trade Organisation (WTO), the Economic Cooperation Organisation (Economic Cooperation Organisation: ECO). In this organisation these countries are included: Pakistan, Iran and Turkey (before it its name was: Regional Cooperation for Development (Regional Cooperation for Development: RCD)), the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation: SAARC); further, trade relations are also being promoted with the Muslim republics (Republics) of Central Asia. Their detailed mention has been made further ahead.

11. Provision of modern facilities

The government has provided some new facilities in this connection, e.g.:

i) To encourage increasing the export of non-traditional products and gaining access to new markets, the government has given a twenty-five per cent subsidy in freight (Freight Subsidy) on exports.

ii) Special export zones (one in Karachi and the second in Punjab) will be established, whose infrastructure will be most modern. These will mostly fulfil the needs of the textile sector, and

iii) In Karachi and Faisalabad garment cities (Garment City) will be established, which will provide a one-window facility (One-Window Facility) to small-level business people.

(continued from p.259) (b) paying attention to those areas which Pakistani exporters have till now ignored, e.g. Africa, Latin America, Eastern Europe, Central Asia and the Far East.

6. Cotton Export Corporation (Cotton Export Corporation)

The Government of Pakistan established this corporation in November 1973 for the export of cotton, which has played an important role in increasing the export of local cotton.

7. Trade relations with Muslim countries

The Government of Pakistan has tried very much to promote trade relations with the Muslim countries of Asia and Africa. Thus our trade with Islamic countries is increasing.

8. Finance for the export of local machinery

To increase the export of machinery prepared within the country, the State Bank, through commercial banks, provides loans at a low rate of interest to traders exporting such machinery, because of which the export of such machinery has been encouraged.

9. Import of machinery

Industries preparing exportable goods (e.g. textiles, leather, sports goods, surgical instruments, utensils, cutlery and furniture) have been given permission to import machinery from outside on paying 35 per cent duty. In this way the export capacity of these industries will increase.

10. Membership of world trade organisations

Pakistan has adopted the membership of different world trade organisations so that it can promote its trade. Among them these are especially noteworthy: the General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs (GATT), the World Trade Organisation (WTO), the Economic Cooperation Organisation (Economic Cooperation Organisation: ECO). In this organisation these countries are included: Pakistan, Iran and Turkey (before it its name was: Regional Cooperation for Development (Regional Cooperation for Development: RCD)), the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation: SAARC); further, trade relations are also being promoted with the Muslim republics (Republics) of Central Asia. Their detailed mention has been made further ahead.

11. Provision of modern facilities

The government has provided some new facilities in this connection, e.g.:

i) To encourage increasing the export of non-traditional products and gaining access to new markets, the government has given a twenty-five per cent subsidy in freight (Freight Subsidy) on exports.

ii) Special export zones (one in Karachi and the second in Punjab) will be established, whose infrastructure will be most modern. These will mostly fulfil the needs of the textile sector, and

iii) In Karachi and Faisalabad garment cities (Garment City) will be established, which will provide a one-window facility (One-Window Facility) to small-level business people.

(1) Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO)

(2) South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation: SAARC (SAARC)

(3) World Trade Organisation (WTO)

Regional and international organisations and their role with reference to Pakistan (Regional and International Organisations and Their Role Towards Pakistan)

At this time some economic organisations exist at the regional and international level which are striving for harmony, progress and prosperity in economic, social and cultural fields through the mutual partnership and cooperation of member countries. These are included among these organisations:

(1) Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO)

(2) South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation: SAARC (SAARC)

(3) World Trade Organisation (WTO)

Here we mention them separately:

Economic Cooperation Organisation (Economic Cooperation Organization: ECO)

In 1964 the then President of Pakistan, General Ayub Khan (late), together with Pakistan’s two neighbouring Muslim countries, Iran and Turkey, established an organisation whose name was kept: “Regional Cooperation for Development” (Regional Cooperation for Development: RCD). Thus between the three countries, because of being neighbours and Muslims, deep relations and connection exist for mutual cooperation. They passed through stages of development in the economic sector. However, in mid-1985 the name of this organisation was changed and, instead of RCD, was kept the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO). Further, besides its first three members, i.e. Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, six states of Central Asia (which became free from Russia) were also included, whose names are these: Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan. Later the neighbouring country Afghanistan was also included. Thus now the number of members of this organisation has become ten.

Objectives of the organisation

Basically the organisation was established for these purposes:

i) mutual trade between member countries should be promoted;

ii) by using natural and economic resources under joint plans, the paths of development should be opened;

iii) with the help of joint capital such industries should be established as are useful for member countries and necessary for prosperity. Thus in this connection economic plans have been made. Measures are being taken to further promote cooperation in economic, industrial, commercial, educational and cultural fields. Trade delegations of member countries make tours of one another. A plan to pass a pipeline through Pakistan to deliver gas from Iran to India is under action.

2. SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation: SAARC)

This organisation was established in 1985. Its members are these countries: Pakistan, Bangladesh, India, Bhutan, Nepal, the Maldives and Sri Lanka. In April 2007, when its fourteenth conference took place, Afghanistan too was made its member. Thus at this time this organisation has eight members. Its head office is in Kathmandu, the capital of Nepal, and the total population of its member countries is approximately one and a half arab.
